source: Written for history/y3 lesson 13 (BC and AD timeline strip and empire outline map (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 13: Rome: from a city to an empire. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

blocks.text: Mark: Rome founded (753 BC), Julius Caesar's raids on Britain (55 and 54 BC), the Roman invasion of Britain (AD 43), Hadrian's Wall begun (AD 122), the Romans leave Britain (about AD 410). Negative numbers are BC.

panels.title: Where is Rome?
points: In Italy, on the River Tiber

timeline.label: AD 117
timeline.text: The empire is at its largest

panels.title: The empire at its biggest
points: From Britain to Egypt and beyond

keywords.def: many lands ruled by one powerful ruler or city
the sea between Europe, Africa and Asia

questions.q: Which sea did the Roman Empire surround?
Which comes first: AD 43 or 27 BC?

questions.a: Strong army, roads, trade or taxes

questions.q: Core: Put six dates on a BC and AD timeline: 753 BC, 55 BC, 27 BC, AD 43, AD 117, AD 410.
Extend: Colour the empire in AD 117 on the map sheet and label Rome, Britain and Egypt.
Stretch: Why might people in conquered lands not want Roman rule?
questions.a: They lost their freedom, had to pay taxes and obey Roman laws
B) 753 BC. In BC, bigger numbers are further back; AD dates come after all BC dates.

questions.q: The Roman Empire was biggest around:
Big question: how could one city rule so much land?
questions.a: A strong army conquered lands, and roads, trade and taxes paid for more
